text:
arjun: quick heads-up — running the kv-cache throughput bench and seeing RSS drift on the server VMs. ~200MB growth over ~10k requests, doesn't go down between runs. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:
kelly: can you paste the bench command and the machine type? I'll try to repro on canary. :eyes:
arjun: ./bench --workload=kv-cache --conns=128 --qps=500 --seq=512 --duration=10m on rwinf-canary-3 (g5xlarge-ish). same docker image as release-2026-02.
maria: two quick spots to check: 1) is jemalloc background thread enabled? 2) are we hitting repeated arena growth because of large-slab allocations? I saw similar on the embedder tests.
arjun: jemalloc uses default conf for now, no explicit MALLOC_CONF. how do I check arena growth at runtime?
maria: run this inside the process:
```c
/* from gdb/python hooking mallctl */
size_t epoch = 1;
mallctl("epoch", NULL, NULL, &epoch, sizeof(epoch));
size_t active;
mallctl("stats.allocated", &active, &(size_t){sizeof(active)}, NULL, 0);
printf("allocated=%zu", active);
```
or just build with jemalloc bookkeeping and call mallctl from a tiny test helper. also mallctl("arenas.purge") can help trigger reclaiming for a check.
sam: another quick repro: try bench with MALLOC_CONF="metadata_thp:disabled, background_thread:true" and compare rss. sometimes THP + fragmentation causes the kernel to keep anon mappings.
kelly: repro attempt queued — pinging eng-infra for a canary with same kernel (5.15) + config. ci-bot: run 1767000000-kvbench-canary job submitted: <https://ci.internal/1767000000/kvcache-repro|job link>
arjun: thanks. I grabbed an smaps snapshot after 5m, pasted the biggest anon mappings below — looks like a handful of large anonymous regions ~64MB each that only grow: total anon ~1.9GB.
kelly: can you attach the smaps snippet and the perf map? also try a quick gcore when it's at peak; a heapshot helps.
arjun: attaching snippet (truncated):
```
AnonHugePages:   65536 kB
Rss:           1953920 kB
...
7f2b00000000-7f2b04000000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0
7f2b20000000-7f2b24000000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0
```
maria: looks like arena growth + big slab allocations. if you can repro with MALLOC_CONF forcing per-thread arenas down (narenas:1) that'd isolate whether fragmentation is from many arenas. little caveat: lowering arenas can increase contention — ok for smoke.
sam: also try MADV_FREE vs MADV_DONTNEED on reclaim path. some kernels only account MADV_FREE lazily which won't drop RSS immediately.
kelly: infra responded — canary ready (rwinf-canary-3). ops-bot: rwinf-canary-3 provisioned, kernel=5.15.0-101-generic, docker 24.0.2.
kelly: i'll run two variants back-to-back: (A) baseline, (B) MALLOC_CONF="narenas:1,background_thread:true,metadata_thp:disabled". will collect smaps, pmap, and a jemalloc epoch dump every 2m.
arjun: perfect. if B shows less steady drift we can land a short-term MALLOC_CONF in the runtime image and open a follow-up to tune arenas + slab sizes.
maria: if we see big improvement, also run a quick flamegraph of malloc hotspots (heap profiler) — might reveal a hot allocation site driving the slabs.
kelly: starting runs now. will post short summary + artifacts here when done. :thumbsup:
